nodes.label: Operator
nodes.description: The developer/orchestrator running es-view locally. Here they right-click a model item in the SPA (a node sticky, a flow, or a hotspot card) and attach a persistent human note to it, then read those notes back in the dialog and via a connected Claude session's grounded context.

nodes.label: AddComment
nodes.description: Attach a human comment/note to a specific model item (node, flow, or hotspot), keyed by the item's stable type:id so it survives model regeneration. The note is recorded in the server's in-memory comment store and written through to a comments.json sidecar next to the model.

tactical.explanation: Trigger: the operator right-clicks any addable item; ContextMenu renders a '💬 Add comment' button whose click calls openCommentDialog(x,y,ref) (ContextMenu.jsx openComments). CommentDialog.submit() trims the textarea and calls addCommentTo(type,id,text) (store.jsx), which POSTs to /api/comments via api.js addComment (fetch POST { type, id, text }). The server /api/comments handler delegates to the addComment command (application/commands/add-comment.ts), which validates the target exists and the text is non-empty (see the two invariants), then calls store.add(type,id,text) and returns store.get(type,id) as the fresh list. The CommentStore class (domain/comment-store/comment-store.ts) implements add(): it builds { id: randomUUID().slice(0,8), text: String(text).trim(), at: new Date().toISOString() }, appends it under the 'type:id' key in the in-memory byKey Map, and calls onChange() — wired by the fs comment-repository adapter (adapters/fs/comment-repository.ts) to persist the sidecar. This is a UI-driven write flow; the SPA runs in a browser served by the same es-view process, so no external service is crossed.

anchors.note: guard target+text then store.add(...); returns store.get(...)

nodes.label: Comment Store
nodes.description: The human-comments boundary: an in-memory Map of 'type:id' -> [{ id, text, at }] created per server run, mirrored to a comments.json sidecar next to the model. It deliberately lives OUTSIDE flows.json (which the recovery/merge pipeline regenerates and would wipe) and keys every note by the item's stable type:id so comments survive a model rebuild. It receives AddComment/RemoveComment and emits CommentAdded; its write to disk is best-effort.

tactical.explanation: The pure CommentStore class (domain/comment-store/comment-store.ts) holds the in-memory byKey Map; load(doc) reproduces it from a prior sidecar doc. add(type,id,text) appends a record under key(type,id) = `${type}:${id}`, throws EmptyCommentError on blank text, and calls onChange(); remove() filters by comment id and re-calls onChange(). The fs comment-repository adapter (adapters/fs/comment-repository.ts) wires onChange to persist(), which serializes { version: 1, comments } (only non-empty lists) via fs.writeFileSync, and on load seeds the store from an existing sidecar (a corrupt file is swallowed and the store starts empty rather than crashing); on any write error it logs once (warned flag) and keeps the comment in memory for the session. The store is wired in adapters/cli/es-view.ts's runView: commentsPath = path.dirname(resolved.sourcePath)/comments.json (i.e. next to flows.json), passed into buildServices as services.comments and shared by the HTTP API and the MCP handler.

anchors.note: in-memory byKey Map; the aggregate's state
warned flag; seeds byKey from existing sidecar; wires onChange -> persist
build record, append under type:id key, calls onChange()

fields.name: key
fields.derivation: The map key under which an item's comments are stored, composed as `${type}:${id}` from the item's kind (node/flow/hotspot) and its STABLE model id. Because the id is stable across model regeneration and the store is a sidecar (not inside the regenerated flows.json), comments re-attach to the same item after a rebuild. This is a design property of the store, not a runtime-checked guard.

fields.name: text
fields.derivation: The human note body, trimmed of surrounding whitespace at record time.

fields.name: id
fields.derivation: Per-comment identifier, the first 8 chars of a randomUUID(). Used to target a specific comment for deletion within an item's list.

fields.name: at
fields.derivation: ISO-8601 creation timestamp (new Date().toISOString()); the dialog and grounded markdown render only the yyyy-mm-dd prefix.

nodes.label: A comment must target an existing model item
nodes.description: ERROR-level guard: AddComment is rejected unless its { type, id } resolves to a real model item — a flow id, a hotspot id, or a node id. A missing id or an unknown item returns HTTP 404 and no comment is recorded. This keeps the sidecar's type:id keys pointing at items the model actually contains.

tactical.explanation: In the addComment command (application/commands/add-comment.ts), the body's type defaults to 'node' by the route; if !id or !itemExists(services, type, id) the command returns a not-found status, which the server route maps to HTTP 404 before store.add is reached. itemExists (application/read-models/items.ts) checks services.model.flows for a flow, services.indexes.hotspotById for a hotspot, else services.indexes.nodeById for a node. Enforced in the command handler rather than inside the CommentStore class, but it is the comment-store boundary's guard.

anchors.note: not-found status when !itemExists, mapped to HTTP 404 by the route

nodes.label: A comment's text must be non-empty
nodes.description: ERROR-level guard: AddComment with blank/whitespace-only text is rejected with HTTP 400 'empty comment' and nothing is stored. The SPA also disables the submit button and returns early on empty text, and the store trims again at record time, but the server 400 is the authoritative rejection.

tactical.explanation: The addComment command (application/commands/add-comment.ts) computes trimmed = (text || '').trim(); if !trimmed it returns an invalid status with error 'empty comment', which the server route maps to HTTP 400, before store.add is reached. The CommentStore class itself also enforces this invariant defense-in-depth: add() throws EmptyCommentError when the trimmed text is blank (domain/comment-store/comment-store.ts) — the shared home for the text-nonempty rule regardless of caller. Defense in depth: CommentDialog.submit returns early when text.trim() is falsy and the 'Add comment' button is disabled on !text.trim().

anchors.note: invalid status 'empty comment' before store.add, mapped to HTTP 400 by the route
EmptyCommentError thrown on blank trimmed text (domain invariant)
early-return on empty; button disabled on !text.trim()

nodes.label: CommentAdded
nodes.description: A human note has been attached to a model item: a { id, text, at } record now hangs under the item's stable type:id key in the comment store. This fact holds as soon as the in-memory Map is updated, independently of whether the write-through to comments.json on disk succeeds.

tactical.explanation: Realized inside CommentStore.add: byKey.set(k, [...(byKey.get(k)||[]), comment]) records the note in memory, then onChange() (wired by the fs comment-repository adapter to persist()) attempts the sidecar write. The handler returns store.get(type,id) (the fresh list) with HTTP 200; store.jsx setItemComments folds it into the SPA `comments` state so the dialog re-renders. The in-memory update always succeeds and is what the API confirms; durability is best-effort.

anchors.note: byKey.set appends the record in memory (the fact)
onChange() best-effort write-through, wired to persist() by the fs adapter

nodes.label: Item comments (dialog + grounded context)
nodes.description: The list of human notes for an item, read back in two places: the SPA CommentDialog (each note's text and yyyy-mm-dd date, with a delete ✕) and the grounded markdown a connected Claude session receives via MCP — every node/flow/hotspot context block appends a 'Comments (human notes)' section. This is how a browser-side note becomes visible to Claude.

tactical.explanation: SPA: on load store.jsx getComments() hydrates the `comments` map ({ 'type:id': [...] }); commentsFor(type,id) feeds CommentDialog's list, and each AddComment/RemoveComment response refreshes just that key via setItemComments. Server GET /api/comments calls the listComments query (application/queries/list-comments.ts), which returns store.all() or store.get(type,id). MCP/grounded context: application/read-models/context.ts attaches services.comments.get('node'|'flow'|'hotspot', id) onto each context object and renderComments() emits the '**Comments (human notes):**' bullet list into the markdown rendered for the model.

nodes.label: Connected Claude (MCP client)
nodes.description: A Claude session connected to the es-view MCP endpoint over the shared in-memory state. It reads the operator's human comments as part of an item's grounded markdown context, so a note added by clicking in the browser rides into what Claude sees.

tactical.explanation: createMcpHandler(services, selection, bundle) (adapters/cli/es-view.ts) is built from the SAME services bundle passed to createServer, so it shares services.comments with the HTTP API; the context renderers (application/read-models/context.ts) fold each item's comments into the grounded markdown the MCP tools return.

anchors.note: createMcpHandler(services, selection, bundle) shares the comment store via services

nodes.label: Local filesystem
nodes.description: The local filesystem outside the process, reached through node:fs. Holds the resolved model source and, alongside it, the comments.json sidecar this flow reads and writes. May be read-only for the bundled example inside a global npx install, in which case writes are swallowed and comments stay in memory.

tactical.explanation: The fs comment-repository adapter (adapters/fs/comment-repository.ts) uses node:fs directly: existsSync + readFileSync to seed the store, writeFileSync to persist. The es-view CLI derives the sidecar path from the resolved model source dir.

nodes.label: comments.json (sidecar)
nodes.description: The persistent sidecar written next to the model (dirname(resolved.sourcePath)/comments.json). Envelope: { version: 1, comments: { "type:id": [ { id, text, at } ] } }. Deliberately separate from flows.json so the recovery/merge pipeline that regenerates the model does not wipe human notes. On load a corrupt file is ignored and the store starts empty.

tactical.explanation: persist() (adapters/fs/comment-repository.ts) writes JSON.stringify({ version: 1, comments }, null, 2) via fs.writeFileSync(filePath). Only non-empty comment lists are serialized. createCommentStore reads the sidecar back with JSON.parse(readFileSync(filePath,'utf8')) and calls store.load(doc) (domain/comment-store/comment-store.ts) to hydrate byKey from doc.comments.

anchors.note: seed byKey from existing sidecar; corrupt => empty

nodes.label: "type:id" (map key)
nodes.description: Object key under comments{} grouping one item's notes, formed as `${type}:${id}`. Stable across model regeneration, which is why sidecar notes re-bind to the same item after a rebuild.

nodes.label: id
nodes.description: Per-comment id, randomUUID().slice(0,8); the delete key within an item's list.

nodes.label: at
nodes.description: ISO-8601 creation timestamp; rendered as yyyy-mm-dd in the UI and grounded markdown.

flows.name: Operator adds a persistent comment to a model item
flows.summary: From the explorer SPA the operator right-clicks any node, flow, or hotspot and adds a human note. The SPA POSTs it to /api/comments, which rejects it unless the target item exists and the text is non-empty, then records it in the server's in-memory comment store keyed by the item's stable type:id and writes through to a comments.json sidecar next to the model. The sidecar lives outside flows.json on purpose, so notes survive the recovery/merge pipeline regenerating the model. The note is read straight back in the dialog and also folded into the grounded markdown a connected Claude session sees.
flows.trigger: Operator clicks '💬 Add comment' in the right-click ContextMenu of a node/flow/hotspot, types a note, and presses Enter (ContextMenu.jsx:50 -> CommentDialog submit).
